items.title: Roscoe Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2023
items.q: So I recall Dexter Gordon was there playing and you know a spring broke on his horn and he needed a rubber band and I just happened to have a rubber band with me ... you know, so I gave him that. I mean I guess the next time I saw Dexter was like when the Art Ensemble went to Europe, so he was there

ctx.x: All right. I want to take you back a little bit before that and I read that in 1961 you had what this review said, a hard bop group and Joseph Jarman and Anthony Braxton. My question is at that point, in 1961, Coltrane released “My Favorite Things” and Ornette Coleman “Free Jazz,” Max Roach had a “Freedom Suite,” and one of my favorites, Hank Mobley had an LP called “Roll Call.” Was there decision-making for you at that point in your career about your direction? © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

Well you know like yeah, I had, we had times that we would all go to Berlin to join with the Berlin band there and also the band from Orleans, France was there as well. And who should be in the band from Orleans, France but Albert Ayler you know. And Albert, I heard him way back then and the way I chose the saxophone is what is your sound you know, where is your sound you know. Because all the great players, you know they had a sound that they were pursuing you know. But when I heard Albert you know I didn’t know…
